Rock Wren: Rock Wren is a small compact wren with a rounded body, short neck, and a relatively upright stance.
Rock Wren shows overall pale gray-brown to sandy-brown upperparts rather than rich warm rufous tones.
Rock Wren has a noticeably paler throat than the face and back.
Rock Wren has underparts that are light buff to whitish instead of uniformly brown.
Rock Wren shows buff to cinnamon flanks that contrast gently with the paler belly.
Rock Wren often has subtle spotting or mottling across the upper breast rather than a clean plain breast.
Rock Wren has a fairly plain face with only a weak pale eyebrow.
Rock Wren lacks the bold white supercilium that stands out on Bewick Wren and Carolina Wren.
Rock Wren has a slender bill that is slightly longer and more decurved than on House Wren.
Rock Wren has a fine pointed bill that appears dark gray to blackish.
Rock Wren has a relatively long tail for its body size.
Rock Wren shows fine dark barring across the tail.
Rock Wren has tail feathers marked with narrow alternating pale and dark bands rather than large white spots.
Rock Wren lacks the bold white-spotted tail pattern typical of Cactus Wren.

Rock Wren has scapulars and back that are plain sandy-brown with only subtle patterning.
Rock Wren shows a crown that is plain brownish and not strongly striped.
Rock Wren has lores and ear coverts that blend into the face instead of forming a crisp facial pattern.
Rock Wren has a dark eye set in a mostly unmarked pale brown face.

Rock Wren has the throat and upper chest washed pale buff to whitish.
Rock Wren has lower belly feathers that appear pale and lightly marked.
Rock Wren shows warmer cinnamon tones on the sides than on the center of the belly.

Rock Wren lacks the strong warm chestnut back often suggested on Carolina Wren.

Rock Wren has upperwing coverts edged in pale brown with fine dark barring.
Rock Wren shows a softly mottled breast pattern instead of heavy bold spotting.
Rock Wren has a tail that looks narrow and neatly barred from base to tip.
Rock Wren has a pale throat that stands out more clearly than in House Wren.
Rock Wren shows only subdued facial markings, unlike the stronger white eyebrow of Carolina Wren.
Rock Wren has sandy-brown rump and upper tail coverts that merge smoothly with the back.
Rock Wren has underparts that are cleaner and paler than the heavily patterned underparts of Cactus Wren.
Rock Wren lacks the bold white throat stripe and heavy breast markings of Cactus Wren.
Rock Wren combines pale sandy plumage, a weak eyebrow, and a finely barred tail as a distinctive field-mark set.

Common Yellowthroat adult male has a bright yellow border above and below the black facial mask.
Common Yellowthroat has rich yellow underparts extending from the throat through the breast and belly.
Common Yellowthroat has mostly plain olive-green upperparts without strong contrasting patches.

Common Yellowthroat has delicate dark legs that suit its lightweight warbler build.
Common Yellowthroat shows a rounded wing shape rather than long pointed wings.
Common Yellowthroat has a tail that appears fairly short and rounded, not obviously long and drooping.

Common Yellowthroat female shows a bright yellow throat and undertail area against otherwise subdued olive plumage.

Common Yellowthroat has yellow extending well onto the belly instead of being restricted to the throat alone.

Common Yellowthroat has a clean yellow throat that merges smoothly into the yellow breast.

Common Yellowthroat has a shorter-tailed silhouette than Yellow Warbler, which can look longer and more elongated.
Common Yellowthroat has a less rounded black head pattern than Wilson Warbler because the dark area is facial rather than crown-centered.

Common Yellowthroat has a plain olive nape and back rather than a sharply contrasting hood-to-back boundary.

Common Yellowthroat has yellow undertail coverts that stand out against the olive upperparts.
